technical_and_design_decisions: For U1, use the existing Spring XD deployment infrastructure and provide a script or documentation to simplify deployment of Scala-based Spark streaming modules.
For U2, create a new wiki page under the 'Troubleshooting' section with the recommended ulimit setting of 10K and include the exception stack trace as context.
For U3, modify the log pattern in config/xd-container-logger.properties to include the date (e.g., using %d{ISO8601} or similar) and verify the change with a local test.
For U4, introduce a configuration option to run Kafka as a separate process (e.g., using a test helper or embedded server) and update build scripts to support this mode.
For U5, refactor publish-maven.gradle to read dependency versions from dependencies.properties instead of hardcoding them, and ensure backward compatibility.
For U6, extend the test infrastructure from U4 to allow external Kafka broker usage, reducing the in-memory footprint of the build.
For U7, run SonarQube analysis on the current codebase, review all violations, fix those that are relevant and mark the rest as false positives with comments.
For U8, create a sample Spark batch job using Spring XD’s job module structure, including configuration, a simple distributed computation, and a README.
assumptions: The developer is proficient in Java, Scala, Gradle, Spring, Kafka, and Spark.
The existing codebase for Spring XD (or equivalent) is available and buildable.
All user stories are independent and can be implemented in any order.
The development environment includes necessary tools: IDE, build tools, SonarQube instance, Kafka, Spark, etc.
The developer works full-time and estimates are based on a single developer performing all tasks.
Testing for each story is unit/integration testing where applicable, no full system regression test required.
Documentation (wiki, README) is considered part of the development effort.
